newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS -BTPs to draw no comfort from budget.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS -BTPs to draw no comfort from budget.

text.p: Italy's supplementary budget plans, designed with European monetary union in mind, are being treated as a paper-shuffling exercise and will leave BTPs vulnerable to underperformance, analysts said on Thursday.

At the same time, some analysts say a widespread bear market is starting for bonds, in which BTPs will suffer. Some forecasts were for a BTP/Bund yield gap as high as 230 basis points in the months ahead.
"There are no real budget measures included," said Lorenzo Codogno, head of economics and market research in Milan.
Codogno said the budget was largely an anticipation of tax payments and a postponement of payments by the state to local authorities and local entities.
The budget was due for approval after a cabinet meeting on Thursday.
"It's nothing compared to what is really needed to prepare the Italian economy for EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union). It could only disappoint our partners," he said.
This was not a lone view.
"I haven't seen any comment where anyone is suggesting these measures can be seen as anything but dubious," said Adrian Schmidt, interantional economist at Chase in London.
Schmidt saw less downside for BTPs than another analysts but that was not because of Italy's fiscal plans. "I don't think the mini-budget can be seen as positive in any shape or form."

The spread between Italy's 7.75 percent BTP due in November 1996 and the 6.0 percent January 1997 Bund was 187 basis points at 1105 GMT. It has edged up from the low 140s in late January, although in the past couple of weeks it has narrowed sharply from above 215.
Analysts said one big reason why the spread was likely to widen was that with European growth starting to pick up, the Bank of Italy's room to cut interest rates was diminishing.
"Even with very good inflation numbers it's becoming very difficult for Italy to cut rates," said Francesco Giordano, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
"The budget doesn't help," he said.
Giordano said the BTP/Bund gap could widen out to 230 basis points, a target he shared with Codogno of BankAmerica.
Codogno said those kind of levels could be achieved on a one to three month basis.

"There is a clear perception that we have turned the interest rate cycle. We are in the middle of a bear market, so it's rather unlikely that Italy will outperform in this situation," he said. "We might see a gradual deterioration of the spread. I'm not expecting a selloff but clearly we will remain weak."

Schmidt, however, disagreed that a bear market was definitely underway. He also argued that considering the amount of talk there has been about a delay to EMU in recent weeks, BTPs have held up fairly well.

"It (the BTP spread) has actually moved a lot less than you would have expected. For that reason I think there's limited downside unless we get some solid evidence of a delay." He added, "I would doubt we'll see EMU delay fears increase that much."
Nonetheless, there were domestic factors also weighing on the BTP market, analysts said.
Giordano noted that a heavy amount of supply was looming, with some 29.5 trillion lire of BTPs due for redemption in April, along with some 11.5 trillion of CTZs.
An auction of BTPs is scheduled for Friday and Codogno said demand could be light with London markets shut for a holiday.
